en: The Chapter on Similes, Section on Ants.
1. The Question on the Ant’s Limb “Venerable Nāgasena, when you say that ‘one limb of the ant must be taken,’ which is that one limb that must be taken?
“Great King, just as the ant, having made a covering over it and concealed itself, goes out for its food;”
In the same way, great king, a yogin, a practitioner of yoga, having made the covering of the restraint of virtue and having closed off the mind, should go for alms.
By means of the covering of the restraint of virtue, great king, the yogin, the practitioner of yoga, transcends all fears.
This, great king, is one quality that should be adopted from the termite.
This was said, Great King, by the Elder Upasena Vaṅgantaputta:
“Having made the mind a roof of restraint in virtue, the yogi...”
one is liberated from fear. Thus ends the first question concerning the term *upacikāṅga*.
